notes: Smallest possible round-trip for muse: one user prompt, one text-only assistant reply, no tool use, asserting ready→working→ready with TotalTokens > 0 after the turn. Recorded with the INTERACTIVE driver (driver-interactive.sh: `muse --trust-workspace` in a tmux REPL inside a fresh per-run cwd, one send + wait_turn + 5s settle + exit_clean). muse is a single-birth FilesUnderRoot adapter (session id = the session directory basename under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions/<Y>/<M>/<D>/<uuid>/, no hooks) — route_facts/metadata/the permission-profile retained_frame are all written at session start, before any prompt, and are Skip=true bookkeeping, so the session is expected to be discovered born ready, not working (unlike copilot's presession split). turn_start anchors to session_birth on event.kind:"started" (EventType=user_message); turn_end anchors to turn_start on event.kind:"terminal",terminal:"completed" (EventType=turn_done, parser.go parseRunTerminal). teardown anchors to turn_end on exit_clean's graceful `/exit`, which now leaves a real session.end(exit_reason:clean) record (commit 0239a1bd) instead of the prior driver's silent tmux kill-session. Session-birth/pid-bind timing bounds are estimates pending a live recording (see the assessment's caveats), not a measured value.

text: Session appears in ready shortly after the muse TUI finishes launching
muse-bin PID bound via the session's .session.lock held flock fd
Assistant reply completes (run terminal:completed → turn_done) → back to ready; no tool call, never entered waiting
exit_clean's graceful /exit ends the session — process_exited on the session
